title: Comparison during the read
statement: Let $x$ be a finite Boolean input and let $c$ be a configuration with $m$ work tapes. Suppose $r$ and $s$ are distinct tape indices, tape $r$ of $c$ contains the binary representation of $i$, and its head is at position $0$. For any natural number $k\le |x|$ and valid input-head position $ip$, there is a number $T$ such that the reading program, started in its initial reading phase with tape $s$ holding the binary representation of $k$ and input-head position $ip$, reaches the same setup with phase $yes$ if $k=i$ and phase $no$ otherwise. Every configuration at a time $n<T$ lies in the read frame of $c$.
